This notice covers this website (rfernex.github.io), the EconRadar app ([rfernex.github.io/EconRadar/radar](https://rfernex.github.io/EconRadar/radar/)) and my personal tools at rfernex.github.io/Apps. Last updated: 24 November 2026.

Contact: [romain.fernex@sciencespo.fr](mailto:romain.fernex@sciencespo.fr), +33 6 84 16 58 58

## Privacy

**In short:** neither this website nor EconRadar has accounts, cookies, analytics, advertising, tracking or session recording. I collect no personal data about visitors, and I sell or share none. The only personal data EconRadar publishes is the published work of researchers: see *Authors of the papers* below.

**Hosting:** GitHub serves the pages. To do so, GitHub receives your IP address and the usual technical details of your browser's request, and may keep them in its server logs for security. I have no access to those logs. See the [GitHub General Privacy Statement](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement).

**Fonts and scripts:** all fonts and scripts, including the one that displays mathematics (MathJax), are served from this website. No page loads anything from Google Fonts, a content delivery network or any other outside service, so your IP address reaches no one but the host.

**EconRadar:** what you do in the app (saved papers, read marks, notes, followed authors, filters, display settings) is kept in your browser's local storage, on your device only. It is never sent to me or to anyone else. You can delete it at any time by clearing this site's data in your browser. A backup file is created only when you ask for one, and stays on your device. If you choose to connect Zotero in the app's settings, your Zotero API key is stored in your browser, and the references you save are sent directly from your browser to Zotero ([Zotero privacy policy](https://www.zotero.org/support/privacy)).

**Authors of the papers:** EconRadar lists the authors of each paper and gathers, for each author, their papers in the radar, their fields, their co-authors and the institutions given in the papers' records. This is personal data under the GDPR. I am responsible for it (the data controller, contact above).

- *Source:* public bibliographic records of published papers and working papers, from OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar and NBER. Nothing else is collected about authors: no contact details, no private or sensitive information.
- *Purpose and legal basis:* helping researchers find recent work and see who works on what. The legal basis is legitimate interest (GDPR, Article 6(1)(f)): the information describes research the authors chose to publish, and it is shown only in that context.
- *Retention:* an author's information stays as long as one of their papers is listed.
- *Your choices:* if you are an author, you can ask for your information to be corrected, or object to it being shown, by writing to the address above. I will answer within one month.

Followed authors are a reader's own choice: that list stays in the reader's browser, like the rest of the app's data.

**Personal tools:** rfernex.github.io/Apps hosts small tools I made for my own use (time tracking, expenses, PhD applications, Italian, reading and GRE practice). They are not meant for the public and are hidden from search engines. Four of them are published encrypted and open only on my own devices: some of their features send text to outside services (translation, literature search, Zotero, language models), and only for me. Anything typed into them is kept in the browser's local storage on that device and is never sent to me. If sync is turned on, a copy goes, through the GitHub API, to a private GitHub repository chosen by the person using the tool, with their own access token.

**Email:** if you write to me, I use your message and address only to reply, and keep them no longer than the conversation needs.

**Links:** links to journals, publishers, GitHub or LinkedIn take you to sites with their own privacy policies.

**Your rights:** under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR, the EU law on personal data), you can ask to access, correct or delete personal data about you, and object to its use, by writing to the address above. You can also complain to the French data protection authority, the [CNIL](https://www.cnil.fr/en/complaints).

## Content and rights

**This website:** unless stated otherwise, its texts and images are © Romain Fernex and may be shared under the [CC BY-ND 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nd/4.0/) licence (credit the author, no modified versions).

**Papers listed in EconRadar:** the papers, and their abstracts, belong to their authors and publishers. EconRadar does not host or reproduce them: each entry links to the publisher's page and, when one exists, to a legal open-access copy. Bibliographic details (titles, authors, institutions, dates, DOIs, links) come from [OpenAlex](https://openalex.org), [Crossref](https://www.crossref.org), [Semantic Scholar](https://www.semanticscholar.org) and [NBER](https://www.nber.org). Journal names are used only to say where a paper was published: EconRadar has no link with, and is not endorsed by, any journal, publisher or author.

**Abstracts:** abstracts are read only to write each paper's summary and tags. They are never published, in the app or in its data files.

**Removal requests:** if you are an author or a rights holder and want a summary corrected or an entry removed, write to the address above. I will act on it promptly.

## AI-generated summaries

Every research question, contribution, summary, conclusion line and identification line shown in EconRadar is written by a language model (mostly Claude, by Anthropic, and for a few papers free models reached through OpenRouter). Each paper's details name the model used. A paper appears in the app only once a model has summarised it.

These summaries are produced automatically and can contain errors or omissions. They are a guide to decide what to read, not a substitute for the paper. They do not express the views of the authors, the journals or the publishers. Check the paper itself before citing it or relying on it. To report an inaccurate summary, write to the address above.

## Liability

This website and EconRadar are provided free of charge, as they are, without any guarantee of accuracy, completeness or availability. I am not responsible for the content of the external sites they link to.
